title: Chapter frontmatter
description: The YAML frontmatter at the top of every file in content/. Each field becomes a data-* attribute the engine reads.

id.description: Permanent, lowercase, hyphenated. Also the file name and the URL. Never change it; if you must, add the old id to data/aliases.json.

order.description: Position inside the book, such as "9.2". A quoted string, so "9.10" stays 9.10. Insert between two chapters with a third part, such as "9.2.1".

stability.description: How fast the facts go stale. Sets the review schedule: volatile after 3 months, moving after 6, evergreen after 12.

reviewed.description: Year and month of the last full review, quoted, such as "2026-11".

status.description: seed: TL;DR, key ideas and planned visuals only. full: the complete chapter template.

visuals.description: Every visual in the body, as "visual-id:form". The form is the viz component, or the Mermaid diagram type (flowchart, sequence, state and so on).

type.description: chapter (the default), playbook (Book 21: one real use case in one industry) or field-note (Book 22: a real deployment, postmortem or failure).

industry.description: Playbooks and field notes: the industry, such as retail or healthcare.

use_case.description: Playbooks and field notes: the one use case, in a short phrase.

outcome.description: Playbooks and field notes: the result in one line, only as measured.

measured_how.description: Playbooks and field notes: how the outcome was measured (metric, baseline, sample, period).

authors.description: GitHub handles of the people whose work the page describes, if they want to be named. Credits for writing the page come from the git history.

prerequisites.description: Chapter ids to read first. Wanted pages are allowed.

replications.description: Others who tried the same approach and reported back.

by.description: GitHub handle or team (anonymized if needed).

result.description: What they found, including how they measured it.
